板上釘釘.d: Settled; a done deal that won't change.
x: 合約已經簽了，這筆交易板上釘釘了。

s.d: What's done can't be undone; somewhat resigned.
s.z: 現在抱怨已經太遲了，木已成舟。
s.y: It's too late to complain; the ship has sailed.

s.d: Almost certain; a forecast, not a settled fact.
s.z: 有了這份合約，這次得標十拿九穩。
s.y: With this contract in hand, winning the bid is all but certain.

e: sth be still up in the air
sth be up in the air
a.z: 這項決定仍懸而未決。
a.y: The decision is still up in the air.

a.d: Not yet finalized; for plans and documents.
a.z: 計畫還在研擬，尚未定案。
a.y: The itinerary has yet to be finalized, so please wait a moment.

板上釘釘.u: Often 已經是板上釘釘的事; used of results and decisions.

x: 經濟快速成長，伴隨而來的是污染增加。

s.d: Arriving one after another, not necessarily as a result.
s.z: 疫情過後，各種問題接踵而至。
s.y: After the pandemic, one problem after another followed.

s.d: Closely linked; not specifically "following from."
s.z: 我們的健康和周遭環境息息相關。
s.y: Our health is closely bound up with the environment around us.

e: have nothing to do with each other
a.z: 這兩件事互不相干，別混在一起談。
a.y: These two matters are unrelated; don't lump them together.

a.p: fēng mǎ niú bù xiāng jí
a.z: 這兩個問題風馬牛不相及，別硬把它們扯在一起。
a.y: The two issues are totally unrelated; don't drag them together.

伴隨而來.u: Often 伴隨…而來的是…, followed by problems, effects or risks.

褒貶不一.d: Opinions are mixed: some praise it, some criticize it.
x: 這項新政策在民眾之間褒貶不一。

e: be praised and criticized in equal measure
s.d: Praise and blame in equal measure; often about people.
s.z: 這位導演毀譽參半，卻始終有自己的擁護者。
s.y: The director has both admirers and critics, yet always keeps a loyal following.

e: have both good and bad sides
s.d: Good and bad results mixed; about outcomes, not opinions.
s.z: 這家公司的過去好壞參半，有輝煌的成功，也有代價慘痛的失敗。
s.y: The trip was a mixed bag: the scenery was lovely, but the weather was awful.

a.z: 這家診所在當地人之間有口皆碑。
a.y: The clinic has a good reputation among all the locals.

a.z: 這次攻擊遭千夫所指。
a.y: The attack was universally condemned.

e: a mix of cheers and jeers
褒貶不一.u: Used for works, policies and public figures.

冰山一角.d: Only a small, visible part of a much bigger problem.
x: 目前曝光的醜聞，只是冰山一角。

e: just a drop in the bucket
s.d: Stresses how small the amount is; 冰山一角 implies much more lies hidden.
s.z: 和醫院所需相比，這筆捐款只是九牛一毛。
s.y: The donation was just a drop in the bucket compared with what the hospital needed.

e: see only a small part of the whole
judge the whole from a narrow view
s.d: About a limited viewpoint (the viewer), not the thing itself.
s.z: 光看一份報告就下結論，等於管中窺豹。
s.y: Judging by a single report is like seeing the whole through a keyhole.

e: lay/put sb's cards on the table
come clean with sb. about sth
a.d: Telling everything without holding back: the opposite of showing only a tip.
a.z: 經過幾小時詢問，他終於對失蹤的款項全盤托出。
a.y: After hours of questioning, he finally came clean about the missing funds.

a.d: Seeing the whole at a glance; about seeing, not telling.
a.z: 站上山頂，整座城市一覽無遺。
a.y: From the summit, the whole city lies spread out before you.

冰山一角.u: Often follows "only" or "just"; common when exposing scandals or social problems.

x: 不出所料，開學第一天列車又誤點了。

s.d: Something one saw coming; can be used as a noun.
s.z: 把責任推給前任經理是意料中事，沒人感到意外。
s.y: Blaming the previous manager is straight out of the playbook, so nobody was surprised.

s.d: Things turned out exactly as suspected: sure enough.
s.z: 我說會下雨，果不其然，下午就下起大雨。
s.y: I said it would rain, and sure enough, it poured in the afternoon.

a.z: 突然的宣布出乎意料，大家都愣住了。
a.y: The sudden announcement took everyone by surprise.

a.z: 那支弱隊奪冠，讓我跌破眼鏡。
a.y: I was incredulous when the underdog won the championship.

不出所料.u: Often opens a sentence, followed by 果然 or 又; English: predictably, as expected.

不合情理.d: Against both common sense and human feeling; it doesn't add up.
x: 她要求立刻退款的做法不合情理。

s.d: Against common sense; about logic, not necessarily feelings.
s.z: 用低於土地價值的價格賣房子，違反常理。
s.y: It defies common sense to ignore such a clear warning.

s.d: Absurd to the point of being laughable; stronger.
s.z: 他的藉口荒謬可笑。
s.y: His excuse was ludicrous.

a.d: Both reasonable and humane; often praise for an arrangement.
a.z: 公司的補償方案合情合理，大家都能接受。
a.y: The company's compensation plan was fair and reasonable, and everyone could accept it.

a.d: Within what one would normally expect.
a.z: 她訓練得那麼刻苦，獲勝是情理之中的事。
a.y: Given how hard she trained, her victory was only to be expected.

不合情理.u: 情理 covers both feelings and reason, so the phrase means unkind as well as illogical.

不可踰越.d: Impossible or forbidden to cross; said of boundaries, gaps or bottom lines.
x: 雙方立場之間的差距，可說是不可踰越的。

s.d: Stresses how big the gap is; 不可踰越 stresses that it cannot be crossed.
s.z: 兩份草稿有天壤之別。
s.y: The two drafts are worlds apart.

s.d: Impregnable defenses or systems; about defense, not distance.
s.z: 這座城堡固若金湯，從來沒有被攻破過。
s.y: The castle was impregnable and had never been taken.

a.d: As easy as turning over one's hand.
a.z: 有了新軟體，報稅易如反掌。
a.y: With the new software, filing taxes has never been so easy.

a.d: Just one step away from the goal.
a.z: 球隊離冠軍只有一步之遙。
a.y: The team was just one step away from the championship.

不可踰越.u: "An unbridgeable gulf" is the classic use; for red lines, English says inviolable or a line that must not be crossed.

不謀而合.d: Arriving at the same idea or approach without having discussed it.
x: 我們從沒交換過意見，想法卻不謀而合。

s.p: yīng xióng suǒ jiàn lüè tóng
s.d: Great minds think alike; complimentary.
s.z: 我們都替這本書取了同一個書名，英雄所見略同！
s.y: We both picked the same title for the book. Great minds think alike!

e: arrive at the same result by different routes
all roads lead to the same place
s.d: Different routes, same result; about outcomes, not ideas.
s.z: 兩位科學家各自研究，殊途同歸，得到相同的結論。
s.y: The two teams used different methods but arrived at the same result.

a.d: Heading the opposite way from one's goal; more than a disagreement.
a.z: 他嘴上說要省錢，行動卻南轅北轍。
a.y: He says he wants to save money, yet everything he does works against it.

a.d: Each side sticks to its own story.
a.z: 兩人對事發經過各執一詞，警方難以判斷。
a.y: The two men each gave a different account of what happened, leaving the police unable to decide.

e: independently arrive at the same idea
不謀而合.u: Usually 與…不謀而合; the point is that there was no prior agreement.

不偏不倚.d: Taking no side; impartial. Can also mean exactly in the middle or right on target.
x: 好的裁判不偏不倚，不會袒護任何一方。

s.d: Upright and incorruptible; stresses character more.
s.z: 這位法官以公正不阿著稱，從不偏袒有錢人。
s.y: The judge was known for his rectitude and never favored the rich.

s.d: Used for comments and judgments, not actions.
s.z: 持平而論，裁判只有一瞬間可以做出判斷。
s.y: To be fair, the referee had only a split second to decide.

a.z: 這份報告對小公司有失公允。
a.y: The report was not fair to the smaller companies.

e: treat one side better than the other
a.d: Treating two sides differently; often about pay, staffing or resources.
a.z: 老師不該厚此薄彼，應該一視同仁。
a.y: A teacher shouldn't play favorites; everyone should be treated alike.

不偏不倚.u: Often describes referees, judges, reporting or positions; a ball landing right on the line is also 不偏不倚 (English: right on target).

x: 社群媒體對選舉的影響不容低估。

s.d: No trivial matter; stresses seriousness.
s.z: 這份合約一旦出錯，後果非同小可。
s.y: This is no small matter, so please think it over carefully.

e: is not to be sneezed at
s.d: More formal; directly says not to belittle someone or something.
s.z: 這支新創公司的實力不容小覷。
s.y: This start-up's strength should not be taken lightly.

a.z: 這點差異微不足道。
a.y: The difference is trivial.

a.d: Not worth mentioning; more of a value judgment.
a.z: 「謝謝你幫我。」「不值一提。」
a.y: Compared with his effort, these results are not worth mentioning.

不容低估.u: A warning or reminder; often followed by 的力量, 的影響 or 的實力.

不容爭辯.d: Beyond dispute; leaves no room for argument.
x: 證據如此明確，結論不容爭辯。

s.d: Beyond doubt; about certainty, not forbidding argument.
s.z: 規律運動能促進健康，這點無庸置疑。
s.y: It is indisputable that regular exercise improves health.

s.d: Evidence as solid as a mountain.
s.z: 鐵證如山，他無法再狡辯。
s.y: The evidence is irrefutable; he can no longer argue his way out.

a.z: 對於停電原因，眾說紛紜。
a.y: Opinions vary widely on what caused the blackout.

e: be unable to agree on any one view
a.d: So many views that no one can decide.
a.z: 專家意見分歧，讓大眾莫衷一是。
a.y: Experts disagree, and the public cannot tell which view to believe.

不容爭辯.u: Can also describe a domineering tone that permits no objection.

x: 健康的飲食會帶來更健康的生活，這是不言而喻的。

s.d: Self-evident, needing no proof; more academic.
s.z: 對大多數人來說，教育的價值不證自明。
s.y: To most of us, the value of education is self-evident.

s.d: Understood by both sides but left unsaid; implies complicity.
s.z: 他們之間心照不宣。
s.y: There was a tacit understanding between them.

a.d: Can't figure it out however hard one thinks.
a.z: 系統為什麼一直當機，我百思不解。
a.y: I'm flummoxed by why the system keeps crashing.

a.z: 他突然發脾氣，房裡每個人都覺得莫名其妙。
a.y: His sudden anger was inexplicable to everyone in the room.

不言而喻.u: Common pattern: ……是不言而喻的; close to 不證自明 but more about not needing to say it.

x: 對大多數人來說，教育的價值不證自明。

s.d: Understood without being said.
s.z: 健康的飲食會帶來更健康的生活，這是不言而喻的。
s.y: It is self-evident that a healthy diet leads to a healthier life.

s.d: Plain to see; about facts being obvious.
s.z: 他根本沒在聽，這再顯而易見不過了。
s.y: It was beyond obvious that he wasn't listening.

a.z: 他突然發脾氣，房裡每個人都覺得莫名其妙。
a.y: His sudden anger was inexplicable to everyone in the room.

a.z: 她為什麼辭掉這麼好的工作，我實在難以理解。
a.y: Why she quit such a good job is unfathomable to me.

不證自明.u: Formal or academic; used for axioms and widely accepted truths.

不只如此.d: It doesn't stop there; there is more.
x: 房租不斷上漲；不只如此，薪資也幾乎沒有成長。

s.d: The formal written version; calm in tone.
s.z: 這項政策降低了成本，不僅如此，還提升了效率。
s.y: The policy cut costs and, what is more, improved efficiency.

e: and that's not even the half of it
s.d: A rhetorical "far more than that"; strong, often surprised or annoyed.
s.z: 他欠錢不還，豈止如此，還到處說我壞話。
s.y: He didn't repay the loan, and that's not even the half of it: he has been badmouthing me everywhere.

a.z: 討論僅止於此，我們進行下一項。
a.y: Let's let the discussion end there and move on to the next item.

a.d: Deliberately stopping at the right point, not a lack of more.
a.z: 老師只點到為止，剩下的讓學生自己想。
a.y: The teacher only hinted at the point and left the rest for the students to work out.

e: and that's only part of the story
不只如此.u: Used at the start or end of a sentence to add further facts; formal writing prefers 不僅如此.

不只一種方式.d: There is more than one way to do something; no need to stick to a single method.
x: 別擔心格式，要達成目的不只一種方式。

s.p: tiáo tiáo dà lù tōng luó mǎ
s.d: Many roads to the same goal; encouraging, stressing that all get there.
s.z: 別急著選，條條大路通羅馬，哪種方式都行。
s.y: Don't rush to choose; all roads lead to Rome, so any approach will do.

s.p: bā xiān guò hǎi, gè xiǎn shén tōng
s.d: Everyone uses their own special skill to succeed.
s.z: 大家八仙過海，各顯神通，想辦法把任務完成。
s.y: Everyone used their own talents and found their own way to get the job done.

a.d: Only two choices, no third way.
a.z: 別把事情看成非此即彼，其實還有第三種可能。
a.y: Don't see it as either-or; there is a third possibility.

a.d: Having no other option; often resigned.
a.z: 債務壓身，他別無選擇，只好賣掉房子。
a.y: Weighed down by debt, he had no choice but to sell the house.

e: There is more than one way to skin a cat
There is more than one way to do it
不只一種方式.u: A saying used to tell people to relax and not fixate on one approach.

x: 他是個徹頭徹尾的紳士。

s.d: Every bit; more colloquial.
s.z: 那場演出不折不扣是天才之作。
s.y: This is an out-and-out scam.

s.d: Genuine, not fake; not "from start to finish."
s.z: 顧客想確定產品貨真價實。
s.y: Customers want to know the product is the genuine article.

a.d: Not entirely so; politely corrects an overstatement.
a.z: 有錢人就一定快樂嗎？不盡然。
a.y: Are rich people always happy? Not necessarily.

a.z: 他的說法半真半假，不能全信。
a.y: His story is half true and half false, so don't believe all of it.

徹頭徹尾.u: Usually before a noun: an utter failure, a downright lie, a gentleman through and through; mostly negative.

x: 持平而論，裁判只有一瞬間可以做出判斷。

s.d: In all fairness; stresses staying calm.
s.z: 平心而論，這部電影的劇本並不差。
s.y: Speaking dispassionately, the film's script isn't bad at all.

e: judge the matter on its own merits
s.d: Sticking to the matter at hand.
s.z: 我們就事論事，不要扯到個人恩怨。
s.y: Let's stick to the issue and leave personal grudges out of it.

a.z: 主管偏聽偏信，才會做出錯誤的決定。
a.y: The manager believed one side only, which led to a wrong decision.

e: treat one side better than the other
a.z: 老師不該厚此薄彼，應該一視同仁。
a.y: A teacher shouldn't play favorites; everyone should be treated alike.

持平而論.u: Often an aside introducing a more balanced, or contrary, view.

穿鑿附會.d: A far-fetched interpretation that forces unrelated things together.
x: 他說這首詩預言了選舉結果，實在是穿鑿附會。

s.d: Forcing connections; more common and colloquial.
s.z: 把這次失敗歸咎於天氣，未免太牽強附會。
s.y: Blaming the weather for this failure is a stretch.

e: make something up out of thin air
s.d: Making things up out of nothing; worse.
s.z: 這些指控純屬無中生有。
s.y: These accusations are fabricated out of thin air.

a.z: 做研究要實事求是，不能先有結論再找證據。
a.y: Research should seek truth from facts, not start from a conclusion and look for evidence.

a.z: 他表現優異，升為經理是順理成章的事。
a.y: Given his excellent performance, becoming manager was a natural step.

穿鑿附會.u: Often criticizes readings of poems, classics or numerical coincidences; more literary than 牽強附會.

x: 關於他辭職的原因，目前純屬臆測。

s.d: Chasing shadows; about rumors.
s.z: 這些報導捕風捉影，沒有任何證據。
s.y: These reports are groundless speculation with no evidence behind them.

s.d: Without any evidence.
s.z: 無憑無據就指控別人，不太公平。
s.y: It isn't fair to accuse people without any evidence.

a.d: Evidence as solid as a mountain.
a.z: 鐵證如山，他無法再狡辯。
a.y: The evidence is irrefutable; he can no longer argue his way out.

a.z: 他的指控有憑有據，不是空口說白話。
a.y: His accusation is backed by evidence; it's not empty talk.

純屬臆測.u: Used to dismiss rumors or unsupported claims; common in official statements and news.

道德優位.d: Claiming the moral high ground: seeing oneself as more righteous and entitled to judge others.
x: 他自稱道德優位，行為卻不比對手好到哪裡。

e: speak in a stern, righteous tone
s.d: Speaking sternly for justice; usually positive.
s.z: 他義正辭嚴地拒絕了賄賂。
s.y: He turned down the improper request in a stern, righteous tone.

s.d: Thinking oneself always right; broader.
s.z: 他自以為是，認為自己比誰都懂。
s.y: He thinks he knows best and never listens to anyone.

a.z: 越有成就的人，往往越虛懷若谷。
a.y: The more accomplished a person is, the more humble and open-minded they tend to be.

a.d: Belittling oneself too much; the other extreme.
a.z: 別妄自菲薄，你的作品很優秀。
a.y: Don't undervalue yourself; your work is excellent.

道德優位.u: Usually critical, implying self-appointed moral superiority.

大哉問.d: "What a big question!": a weighty question that's hard to answer.
x: 「什麼是美好的人生？」這真是個大哉問。

s.d: An internet coinage for a soul-searching question; sharper.
s.z: 這個問題簡直是靈魂拷問，我答不出來。
s.y: That is a truly soul-searching question, and I can't answer it.

s.d: Thought-provoking; about reflection, not difficulty.
s.z: 這部紀錄片非常發人深省。
s.y: The documentary was deeply thought-provoking.

a.d: The answer is obvious at a glance.
a.z: 袖口上的污漬，一望便知他剛才在刷油漆。
a.y: The answer is obvious at a glance.

a.z: 有了新軟體，報稅易如反掌。
a.y: With the new software, filing taxes has never been so easy.

大哉問.u: Often said with a sigh, or jokingly, when a question can't be answered in a sentence.

x: 他的預測在最終結果出爐後得到驗證。

s.d: Able to withstand scrutiny.
s.z: 好的理論必須經得起檢驗。
s.y: A good theory has to hold up to scrutiny.

s.p: shì shí shèng yú xióng biàn
s.d: Facts speak louder than arguments.
s.z: 銷售數字就在這裡，事實勝於雄辯。
s.y: The sales figures say it all: facts speak louder than words.

a.z: 他的論點根本站不住腳。
a.y: His argument simply doesn't hold water.

a.d: Collapses on its own without needing to be refuted.
a.z: 謠言傳了幾天，不攻自破。
a.y: The rumor fell apart on its own after a few days.

得到驗證.u: Follows predictions, hypotheses or theories; the opposite is 被推翻 (overturned).

等價交換.d: Equivalent exchange: what you give equals what you get.
x: 這是一場等價交換：公司得到減稅，市政府得到一座新公園。

s.d: Returning favors and gifts.
s.z: 外交講究禮尚往來，國事訪問通常會回訪。
s.y: Diplomacy runs on reciprocity: a state visit is usually returned.

s.d: Repaying kindness with kindness.
s.z: 她借我筆記，我就做晚餐投桃報李。
s.y: She lent me her notes, so I reciprocated by cooking dinner.

e: a small outlay for a huge return
a.d: Huge returns on a tiny investment; not equal.
a.z: 世上沒有一本萬利又穩賺的事。
a.y: There is no such thing as a small outlay for a guaranteed huge return.

a.z: 天底下沒有不勞而獲的好事。
a.y: There is no such thing as a free lunch.

等價交換.u: A popular phrase from alchemy and anime; colloquially close to "you reap what you sow."

的確如此.d: That's right; that's exactly how it is.
x: 的確如此，這個專案實質上已經完成，只剩潤飾細節。
他說這家店很好吃，的確如此。
He said the restaurant is great, and that is indeed the case.

s.d: Absolutely true; stronger.
s.z: 他說的千真萬確，我親眼看到的。
s.y: What he says is absolutely true; I saw it with my own eyes.

s.d: Without a doubt; about certainty.
s.z: 毫無疑問，她是球隊裡最好的球員。
s.y: She is indisputably the best player on the team.

a.z: 大家都以為他很有錢，其實並非如此。
a.y: Everyone thinks he is rich, but that is not the case.

a.z: 他不是不努力，恰恰相反，他比誰都用功。
a.y: He isn't lazy; quite the opposite, he works harder than anyone.

的確如此.u: Used to agree with what someone has just said.

二元對立.d: Binary opposition: seeing everything in two opposed categories.
x: 這場辯論已淪為善惡二元對立的較量。

s.d: Either this or that; the everyday version.
s.z: 別把事情看成非此即彼，其實還有第三種可能。
s.y: Don't see it as either-or; there is a third possibility.

s.d: Black and white; sometimes a virtue, sometimes oversimplified.
s.z: 他看事情黑白分明，不留灰色地帶。
s.y: He sees things as clear-cut and leaves no gray area.

a.z: 法律對這種行為存在灰色地帶。
a.y: The law leaves a gray area around this kind of conduct.

a.z: 這所大學兼容並蓄，包容多元觀點。
a.y: The university embraces diverse views.

二元對立.u: Used in social science and commentary to criticize oversimplification.

法網恢恢.d: The net of the law is wide; wrongdoers can't escape.
x: 他以為能騙過稅務機關，卻逃不過法網恢恢。

e: justice will catch up with you
no one escapes in the end
s.d: Heaven's net; implies karma rather than the law.
s.z: 天網恢恢，作惡的人終究逃不掉。
s.y: Justice has a long reach, and wrongdoers will not escape in the end.

s.d: Paid back in this life for one's misdeeds.
s.z: 他騙了所有人，結果自己賠光了錢，真是現世報。
s.y: He cheated everyone and then lost all his money: instant karma.

a.z: 詐騙犯仍逍遙法外。
a.y: The fraudster is still at large.

a.d: A culprit who slipped through the net (a person).
a.z: 警方追捕多日，仍有一條漏網之魚。
a.y: The police hunted for days, but one suspect still slipped through the net.

法網恢恢.u: Full form: 法網恢恢，疏而不漏; used when a criminal is finally caught.

法網恢恢，疏而不漏.d: Justice is slow but sure: no wrongdoer slips through the net.
x: 多年後連最大的黑道老大也落網了，可見法網恢恢，疏而不漏。

e: the wicked get what they deserve
s.d: Evil gets its due, not necessarily through the law.
s.z: 做盡壞事的人，終究惡有惡報。
s.y: Those who do evil will in the end get what they deserve.

s.d: Reaping what one has sown.
s.z: 他欺騙別人，如今自食其果。
s.y: He cheated others, and now he reaps what he sowed.

a.z: 詐騙犯仍逍遙法外。
a.y: The fraudster is still at large.

a.d: Vanishing without a trace; often ironic.
a.z: 歹徒作案後逃之夭夭。
a.y: The criminals fled the scene after the crime.

e: no one slips through the net of the law
the long arm of the law
法網恢恢，疏而不漏.u: From the Laozi (天網恢恢，疏而不失); modern usage swaps heaven for the law.

覆巢之下無完卵.d: When the nest is overturned, no egg stays whole: when the whole collapses, no one is spared.
x: 銀行接連倒閉，大家才明白覆巢之下無完卵。

s.d: Innocent bystanders get hurt; stresses being dragged in.
s.z: 大企業倒閉，小供應商遭受池魚之殃。
s.y: Small suppliers suffered collateral damage when the giant firm went bankrupt.

s.d: Allies who depend on each other: if one falls, the other suffers.
s.z: 兩個鄰國唇亡齒寒，一方倒下，另一方就會暴露在危險中。
s.y: The neighbors share a common fate: if one falls, the other is exposed.

a.z: 他設法從這筆交易中全身而退。
a.y: He managed to just walk away from the deal.

a.z: 車子滑出路面，所幸僥倖脫險，沒有人受傷。
a.y: The car skidded off the road, but it was a close call and nobody was hurt.

覆巢之下無完卵.u: From a story about Kong Rong's children; a reminder that individuals share the fate of their country, company or family.

箇中道理.d: The reasons and logic behind something.
x: 她向大家說明新政策背後的箇中道理。

s.d: The hidden subtleties and tricks.
s.z: 這道菜的好吃，其中奧妙就在火候。
s.y: The secret of this dish lies in the heat control.

s.d: The sequence of events; 箇中道理 is the "why."
s.z: 在你下判斷之前，讓我先說明整件事的來龍去脈。
s.y: Before you judge, let me explain the whole story.

e: not understand what is going on
a.z: 大家都不明所以，只好等他解釋。
a.y: Everyone was baffled and had to wait for his explanation.

e: have only a smattering of knowledge
a.z: 他對這個主題一知半解。
a.y: He has only a smattering of knowledge about the issue, yet loves to give his opinion.

箇中道理.u: Also written 個中道理; often after 明白, 懂得 or 說明.

x: 顧名思義，快閃店只會短暫出現。

e: guess the meaning from the words alone
s.d: Guessing the meaning from the words alone; often misleading.
s.z: 不懂典故就望文生義，很容易解釋錯。
s.y: Guessing the meaning from the words alone, without knowing the allusion, easily leads to errors.

s.d: Clear at a glance; not limited to names.
s.z: 這張圖表一目了然。
s.y: The chart is clear at a glance.

e: not live up to its name
a.d: Not living up to the name.
a.z: 這家「五星級」餐廳名不副實。
a.y: This "five-star" restaurant doesn't live up to its name.

a.d: Far-fetched interpretation; the opposite of natural inference.
a.z: 他說這首詩預言了選舉結果，實在是穿鑿附會。
a.y: His claim that the poem predicted the election is farfetched.

顧名思義.u: Usually opens a sentence as a parenthetical.

好壞參半.d: A mix of good and bad.
x: 這家公司的過去好壞參半，有輝煌的成功，也有代價慘痛的失敗。
這家公司過去好壞參半，既有大成功，也有昂貴的失敗。
The company has a chequered past, with both great successes and costly failures.

e: be praised and criticized in equal measure
s.d: Praise and blame in equal measure; usually about people.
s.z: 這位導演毀譽參半，卻始終有自己的擁護者。
s.y: The director has both admirers and critics, yet always keeps a loyal following.

s.d: Strengths and flaws side by side; formal, often in reviews.
s.z: 這部小說瑕瑜互見，有精采片段也有冗長段落。
s.y: The novel has both strengths and weaknesses: some brilliant passages and some tedious ones.

a.z: 這場演出盡善盡美。
a.y: The performance was flawless.

a.z: 他把自己說得一無是處。
a.y: He talks as if he has not one redeeming quality.

好壞參半.u: Used of results, experiences and performance.

好人有好報.d: Good things happen to good people.
x: 她幫過鎮上每個人，如今大家都來幫她，這就是好人有好報。

s.d: The more formal version, often paired with 惡有惡報.
s.z: 善有善報，他的努力終於有了回報。
s.y: Good deeds are rewarded; his efforts finally paid off.

e: good people are watched over by heaven
s.d: Good people are protected by heaven; often said to comfort.
s.z: 吉人天相，他一定能平安度過難關。
s.y: Good people are watched over by heaven; he will surely get through this safely.

e: the wicked get what they deserve
a.z: 做盡壞事的人，終究惡有惡報。
a.y: Those who do evil will in the end get what they deserve.

a.d: Bad people in power while the good suffer.
a.z: 世風日下，惡人當道。
a.y: The world has gone downhill and the wicked are in power.

e: good things come to those who do good
好人有好報.u: Full saying: 好人有好報，惡人有惡報.

x: 毫無疑問，她是球隊裡最好的球員。

s.d: The formal equivalent.
s.z: 規律運動能促進健康，這點無庸置疑。
s.y: It is indisputable that regular exercise improves health.

s.d: Absolutely true; stronger.
s.z: 他說的千真萬確，我親眼看到的。
s.y: What he says is absolutely true; I saw it with my own eyes.

e: take sth. with a grain of salt
a.z: 他的承諾，我聽了半信半疑。
a.y: I took his promise with a grain of salt.

a.z: 他突然改口，啟人疑竇。
a.y: The sudden change in his story raised suspicion.

毫無疑問.u: Often an adverb at the start of a sentence; means the same as 無庸置疑 but is more conversational.

x: 要在今晚前寫完報告，很不可能。

s.d: As hard as climbing to the sky; hyperbolic.
s.z: 下雨的尖峰時段要叫到計程車難如登天。
s.y: Finding a taxi at rush hour in the rain is insanely difficult.

s.d: So slim it's almost zero; often about odds.
s.z: 風險微乎其微。
s.y: The risk is negligible.

a.d: Done with no effort at all.
a.z: 對他來說，這只是輕而易舉的小事。
a.y: For him, this is a piece of cake.

a.z: 有了這份合約，這次得標十拿九穩。
a.y: With this contract in hand, winning the bid is all but certain.

很不可能.u: A conversational phrase; formal writing tends to use 幾乎不可能.

核心原則.d: A core principle: the most important, unshakable rule.
x: 誠實是新聞工作的核心原則。

s.d: Golden rules; sounds authoritative, even sacred.
s.z: 「顧客至上」是我們店裡的金科玉律。
s.y: "The customer comes first" is the golden rule in our shop.

s.d: The number-one rule.
s.z: 口譯的首要規則，是忠實傳達說話者的原意。
s.y: The cardinal rule of interpreting is to stay faithful to the speaker's meaning.

a.z: 我們六點還是七點見面都無關緊要。
a.y: Whether we meet at six or seven is immaterial.

a.z: 別在枝微末節上花太多時間。
a.y: Don't spend too much time on trivial details.

核心原則.u: 核心 goes before nouns, as in 核心價值 and 核心原則.

話不投機半句多.d: When you don't get along, even half a sentence is too much.
x: 爭了十分鐘後，我明白我們話不投機半句多，便不再開口。

s.p: dào bù tóng bù xiāng wéi móu
s.d: People with different goals can't work together.
s.z: 他選擇不與價值觀和自己相反的人往來，道不同不相為謀。
s.y: We want different things, so we should go our separate ways.

e: be like a fish out of water
s.d: Out of place; not fitting in.
s.z: 在古板的辦公室裡，那位年輕設計師顯得格格不入。
s.y: He felt like a fish out of water among his new colleagues.

a.z: 我們喝咖啡時相談甚歡。
a.y: We had a nice talk over coffee.

a.p: jiǔ féng zhī jǐ qiān bēi shǎo
e: good company makes the drinks flow
a.d: With a kindred spirit, a thousand cups aren't enough.
a.z: 酒逢知己千杯少，我們聊到天亮。
a.y: With a kindred spirit, no amount of drinks is too much; we talked until dawn.

e: we don't speak the same language
have nothing to say to each other
話不投機半句多.u: Full couplet: 酒逢知己千杯少，話不投機半句多.

家家有本難念的經.d: Every family has its own troubles.
x: 看起來大家都很幸福，其實家家有本難念的經。

s.p: qīng guān nán duàn jiā wù shì
e: even an upright magistrate can't settle family quarrels
s.d: Outsiders can't judge family quarrels.
s.z: 清官難斷家務事，這種事外人別插手。
s.y: Even an upright magistrate can't settle family quarrels; outsiders shouldn't interfere.

e: have something one can't speak of
s.d: A difficulty one can't talk about.
s.z: 他不肯多說，大概有難言之隱。
s.y: He won't say more; he probably has something he can't speak of.

a.z: 他們享受了五十年的家庭幸福。
a.y: To him, domestic bliss is worth more than any promotion.

a.z: 俗話說，家和萬事興。
a.y: As the saying goes, a harmonious family prospers.

e: every family has its own troubles
家家有本難念的經.u: Often said to remind people not to envy others' seemingly perfect lives.

見樹不見林.d: Can't see the forest for the trees: lost in details, missing the big picture.
x: 他盯著小錯字，見樹不見林。

s.d: Generalizing from a part; a faulty judgment.
s.z: 憑一個觀光客就評斷整個國家，是以偏概全。
s.y: Rejecting everything because of one failure is a sweeping generalization.

e: see only a small part of the whole
judge the whole from a narrow view
s.d: A limited view; about the viewer.
s.z: 光看一份報告就下結論，等於管中窺豹。
s.y: Judging by a single report is like seeing the whole through a keyhole.

a.d: Far-sighted, with the big picture in mind.
a.z: 一位好的領導者必須高瞻遠矚。
a.y: A good leader must take the long view.

a.d: Seeing what's coming before it happens.
a.z: 她洞燭機先，早在股市崩盤前就看出端倪。
a.y: She could see it coming long before the market crashed.

e: can't see the forest for the trees
見樹不見林.u: From 只見樹木，不見森林; describes a lack of perspective.

加以證明.d: To prove something with facts, data or reasoning.
x: 延後上課的主張，已有數據加以證明。

s.d: Proven after testing; from the side of what gets proven.
s.z: 他的預測在最終結果出爐後得到驗證。
s.y: His prediction was borne out by the final results.

s.d: Backed by evidence.
s.z: 他的指控有憑有據，不是空口說白話。
s.y: His accusation is backed by evidence; it's not empty talk.

a.z: 空口無憑，請給我書面證明。
a.y: Words alone prove nothing; please give me written proof.

a.z: 他說他徒手抓到一條鯊魚，聽起來根本是無稽之談。
a.y: That claim is sheer nonsense.

加以證明.u: 加以 is a formal auxiliary followed by a two-character verb.

既成事實.d: A fait accompli: something that has already happened and can't be changed.
x: 董事會面對的是既成事實：大樓早已賣掉。

s.d: Spilled water can't be gathered up.
s.z: 覆水難收，說出口的話收不回來。
s.y: What's done can't be undone, and spoken words can't be taken back.

s.d: Beyond saving.
s.z: 森林受到的破壞難以挽回。
s.y: The damage to the forest is irreparable.

e: sth be still up in the air
sth be up in the air
a.z: 這項決定仍懸而未決。
a.y: The decision is still up in the air.

a.d: There's still room for negotiation or change.
a.z: 這次談判幾乎沒有轉圜空間。
a.y: There is little room to maneuver in the negotiations.

既成事實.u: Common in 面對既成事實 (face a fait accompli) and 造成既成事實 (present a fait accompli).

x: 這對兄弟的個性截然不同。

s.d: Far apart; very different.
s.z: 兩人的看法大相逕庭。
s.y: The two have very different views.

s.d: A world of difference; stresses the size of the gap.
s.z: 兩份草稿有天壤之別。
s.y: The two drafts are worlds apart.

e: be cut from the same cloth
a.d: Exactly alike, as if from the same mold.
a.z: 這兩幅畫的風格如出一轍。
a.y: The two paintings are in exactly the same style.

a.d: Largely the same, with minor differences.
a.z: 這兩份提案大同小異。
a.y: The two proposals are much the same.

積非成是.d: A wrong repeated long enough comes to be accepted as right.
x: 若一直放著這個錯誤不管，終將積非成是。

s.d: A rumor that gets more distorted as it spreads; stresses spreading.
s.z: 大家沒查證就轉貼，以訛傳訛。
s.y: People shared the post without checking and spread misinformation.

s.d: Deliberately calling black white.
s.z: 他在會議上指鹿為馬，把錯誤說成正確。
s.y: He called a deer a horse in the meeting, passing off the wrong as right.

a.z: 臨時政府的首要任務就是撥亂反正，恢復秩序。
a.y: The interim government's first task was to restore order and set things right.

e: get to the root and set things right
a.d: Fixing a problem at its root.
a.z: 要解決問題，就得正本清源。
a.y: To solve the problem, we must tackle it at the root.

e: a lie repeated often enough becomes truth
積非成是.u: A warning not to tolerate small errors.

經得起檢驗.d: Able to stand up to scrutiny.
x: 好的理論必須經得起檢驗。

s.d: Gaining value over time; about time.
s.z: 她的設計歷久彌新。
s.y: Her designs are timeless.

s.d: Flawless.
s.z: 辯護律師的邏輯無懈可擊。
s.y: Her argument was flawless.

a.z: 他的論點根本站不住腳。
a.y: His argument simply doesn't hold water.

a.z: 這支球隊看似強大，實際上不堪一擊。
a.y: The team looks strong but crumbles at the first blow.

經得起檢驗.u: Often with 時間, 事實 or 公評, as in 經得起時間的檢驗 (stand the test of time).

經驗法則.d: A rule of thumb drawn from experience; practical but not exact.
x: 依經驗法則，國際航班要提前兩小時到機場。

s.d: A convention that arose from long habit.
s.z: 這個規則已經約定俗成。
s.y: The rule has become established by convention.

s.d: A lesson from others' past mistakes.
s.z: 歷史上有許多前車之鑑。
s.y: History offers many cautionary examples.

a.z: 關於他辭職的原因，目前純屬臆測。
a.y: Why he resigned is still pure guesswork.

a.z: 做產品不能閉門造車，要多聽用戶意見。
a.y: You can't build products in isolation; listen to your users.

經驗法則.u: A rough working guide, not a scientific law.

金科玉律.d: A golden rule that must not be broken.
x: 「顧客至上」是我們店裡的金科玉律。

s.d: A wise saying; about words, not rules.
s.z: 他把父親的至理名言牢記在心。
s.y: He keeps his father's words of wisdom firmly in mind.

s.d: The number-one rule; 金科玉律 stresses that it's inviolable.
s.z: 口譯的首要規則，是忠實傳達說話者的原意。
s.y: The cardinal rule of interpreting is to stay faithful to the speaker's meaning.

a.d: A rule that exists only on paper.
a.z: 這條規定形同虛設。
a.y: The rule is a dead letter.

a.z: 要解決這個問題，我們得打破常規。
a.y: To solve this problem, we need to think outside the box.

金科玉律.u: Originally precious legal texts; now creeds in a trade or in life.

緊密關連.d: Closely connected; bound up with each other.
x: 在這個議題上，兩位部長的立場緊密關連，看不出任何分歧。
環境與健康緊密關連。
Our health is closely connected with the environment.

s.d: Closely linked; affecting each other.
s.z: 我們的健康和周遭環境息息相關。
s.y: Our health is closely bound up with the environment around us.

s.d: Inseparable.
s.z: 語言與文化密不可分。
s.y: Language and culture are inseparable.

e: have nothing to do with each other
a.z: 這兩件事互不相干，別混在一起談。
a.y: These two matters are unrelated; don't lump them together.

a.d: Of no concern; usually about attitudes or remarks.
a.z: 這些無關痛癢的評論，不必放在心上。
a.y: These inconsequential comments needn't be taken to heart.

緊密關連.u: Also written 緊密關聯; used for cause-and-effect or dependence.

僅止於此.d: That's as far as it goes; nothing more.
x: 討論僅止於此，我們進行下一項。

s.d: That's the end of it; colloquial, can be a warning.
s.z: 今天的會議到此為止。
s.y: That's all for today's meeting.

s.d: Stopping at the right point.
s.z: 老師只點到為止，剩下的讓學生自己想。
s.y: The teacher only hinted at the point and left the rest for the students to work out.

a.d: There's more; it doesn't stop there.
a.z: 房租不斷上漲；不只如此，薪資也幾乎沒有成長。
a.y: That's not all; the price also includes free delivery.

a.z: 霸凌者不但沒有收手，反而變本加厲。
a.y: Instead of stopping, the bullies went from bad to worse.

僅止於此.u: Used to close a topic or limit the scope.

絕無僅有.d: One of a kind; almost unheard of.
x: 從這座山頂看出去的景色，世上絕無僅有。

e: can be counted on one hand
s.d: Very few but countable; 絕無僅有 means almost the only one.
s.z: 這個領域的專家屈指可數。
s.y: Experts in this field can be counted on one hand.

s.d: Unique; stresses being special, not necessarily rare.
s.z: 這件手工藝品獨一無二。
s.y: This handmade piece is one of a kind.

a.z: 報告裡這種錯誤比比皆是。
a.y: Such errors are everywhere in the report.

a.z: 這條路線誤點是司空見慣的事。
a.y: Delays are commonplace on this line.

絕無僅有.u: Often describes opportunities, talent, scenery or experiences; usually positive.

橘逾淮為枳.d: A tangerine planted north of the Huai River becomes a bitter orange: the same thing changes when its surroundings change.
x: 全盤照搬國外的政策，往往橘逾淮為枳。

s.d: Cutting the foot to fit the shoe: forcing an unsuitable method; 橘逾淮為枳 is about change caused by a new environment.
s.z: 為了符合理論而竄改事實，就像削足適履。
s.y: Changing the facts to fit the theory is like using a Procrustean bed.

s.d: Failing to adapt to a new place.
s.z: 這套管理制度一到分公司就水土不服。
s.y: The management system failed to adapt once it reached the branch office.

a.d: Adapting to local conditions: the cure for 橘逾淮為枳.
a.z: 這道食譜因地制宜，配合各地的口味調整。
a.y: Policies should be adapted to local conditions.

e: when in Rome, do as the Romans do
a.d: When in Rome, do as the Romans do.
a.z: 入境隨俗，進門前要脫鞋。
a.y: When in Rome, do as the Romans do: take off your shoes at the door.

e: what works in one place may fail in another
橘逾淮為枳.u: From the Rites of Zhou (Kao Gong Ji); the Yanzi Chunqiu tells a similar story; also 南橘北枳. Now a warning against transplanting systems, policies or management methods wholesale.

可恨之人，必有可憐之處.d: Behind every detestable person lies something to pity.
x: 可恨之人，必有可憐之處：愛傷人的人，往往自己也在受傷。

e: be fierce in appearance but weak within
s.d: Fierce outside, timid inside; bluster.
s.z: 他看起來很兇，其實是色厲內荏。
s.y: He looks fierce but is really weak inside.

s.d: Pretending to be strong to scare others.
s.z: 他的威脅只是虛張聲勢，雷聲大雨點小。
s.y: His threats were just a bluff; he is more bark than bite.

a.z: 她菩薩心腸，見不得別人受苦。
a.y: She has a heart of gold and can't bear to see others suffer.

a.z: 那個反派心狠手辣、冷血無情。
a.y: The villain is ruthless and cold-blooded.

來龍去脈.d: The whole story, from start to finish.
x: 在你下判斷之前，讓我先說明整件事的來龍去脈。

s.d: Cause and effect.
s.z: 你得先弄清楚前因後果，再下結論。
s.y: You must understand the whole chain of cause and effect before drawing a conclusion.

s.d: Told in full detail.
s.z: 他把事情的經過一五一十地告訴了警察。
s.y: He told the police everything that had happened, in full detail.

e: be in the dark about what is going on
a.z: 他不明就裡，貿然插手。
a.y: Being in the dark about what was going on, he rashly stepped in.

a.z: 這張表格讓我一頭霧水。
a.y: I'm baffled by this form.

來龍去脈.u: Often after 說明, 了解 or 釐清.

牢不可破.d: Unbreakable; too strong to be broken.
x: 他們簽了一份牢不可破的協議。

s.d: Impregnable; about defenses.
s.z: 這座城堡固若金湯，從來沒有被攻破過。
s.y: The castle was impregnable and had never been taken.

s.d: Indestructible; for objects or willpower.
s.z: 他的意志堅不可摧。
s.y: His will is indestructible.

a.z: 這支球隊看似強大，實際上不堪一擊。
a.y: The team looks strong but crumbles at the first blow.

a.d: Crumbling at the slightest touch; often of armies or defenses.
a.z: 敵軍士氣低落，一觸即潰。
a.y: The enemy's morale was low, and they collapsed at the first touch.

牢不可破.u: Used for friendships, alliances, contracts and records.

劣幣驅逐良幣.d: Bad money drives out good: the bad crowds out the good.
x: 市場上充斥廉價仿冒品，劣幣驅逐良幣。

s.d: Passing off fakes as genuine; about mixing in, not crowding out.
s.z: 有些賣家魚目混珠，以假亂真。
s.y: Some sellers pass off fakes as genuine.

s.d: Usurping someone else's place.
s.z: 他靠關係進公司，鳩占鵲巢，把原來的人擠走了。
s.y: He got in through connections and pushed out the person who held the post.

a.d: Survival of the fittest: the better ones remain.
a.z: 市場競爭本來就是優勝劣敗。
a.y: Market competition is survival of the fittest.

a.d: Discarding the dross and keeping the best.
a.z: 好的編輯就是去蕪存菁，濾掉雜訊、留下精華。
a.y: Good editing means filtering out the noise to extract the essence.

e: the bad drives out the good
劣幣驅逐良幣.u: The Chinese name for Gresham's law; also used to criticize personnel systems.

另有其人.d: It's someone else; the real person is not the one in front of us.
x: 警方很快發現，真正的兇手另有其人。

s.d: Pinning something on the wrong person.
s.z: 這句名言常被張冠李戴，其實不是他說的。
s.y: This famous line is often attributed to the wrong person; he never said it.

s.d: There's more to the story; about circumstances, not people.
s.z: 他突然辭職，其中另有隱情。
s.y: His sudden resignation has hidden reasons behind it.

e: the evidence of guilt is conclusive
a.z: 罪證確鑿，他只好認罪。
a.y: With the evidence of guilt conclusive, he had no choice but to plead guilty.

a.z: 警方人贓俱獲，當場逮捕嫌犯。
a.y: The police caught the suspect red-handed with the stolen goods.

e: the real culprit is someone else
另有其人.u: Pattern: 真正的……另有其人; used in investigations or when tracking someone down.

邏輯嚴密.d: Watertight logic: each step follows tightly from the last.
x: 她的論證邏輯嚴密，確實具備邏輯上的有效性。

s.d: Unassailable; broader than logic.
s.z: 辯護律師的邏輯無懈可擊。
s.y: Her argument was flawless.

s.d: Tightly linked; also for plots and plans.
s.z: 這部懸疑片情節環環相扣，讓人無法分心。
s.y: The plot of this thriller is so tightly interlinked that you can't look away.

a.z: 他的說詞漏洞百出，沒有人相信。
a.y: His story was full of holes, and nobody believed it.

a.z: 證人的證詞前後矛盾。
a.y: The witness's statements were full of inconsistencies.

邏輯嚴密.u: Praise for arguments, essays or a legal defense.

名符其實.d: Living up to its name; the real thing.
x: 她是名符其實的專家，不只是頭銜漂亮。

s.d: Recognition that is fully deserved.
s.z: 她拿下年度大獎，可說是實至名歸。
s.y: Winning the annual award was well deserved.

s.d: Genuine goods at a fair price; for things or ability.
s.z: 顧客想確定產品貨真價實。
s.y: Customers want to know the product is the genuine article.

a.z: 他這個國王徒具虛名，實權握在議會手裡。
a.y: He was king in name only; the real power rested with the council.

e: cease to exist except in name
a.d: Exists in name only; the substance is gone.
a.z: 這項條約仍留在紙面上，實際上已名存實亡。
a.y: The treaty still exists on paper, but it has ceased to exist except in name.

名符其實.u: Also written 名副其實; both are correct.

x: 只要是我能力所及，我一定幫你。

s.d: Doing one's best without promising results.
s.z: 我會盡力而為，但無法保證成功。
s.y: I'll do my best, but I can't guarantee success.

s.d: Doing only what one can manage, without overreaching.
s.z: 創業要量力而為，不要借太多錢。
s.y: When starting a business, act within your means and don't borrow too much.

a.z: 這項任務他力有未逮。
a.y: The task was beyond his ability.

a.z: 面對這場災難，我們無能為力。
a.y: Faced with this disaster, we were powerless.

能力所及.u: Often 在能力所及的範圍內; when something is beyond one's ability, say 力有未逮.

牛牽到北京還是牛.d: A leopard can't change its spots: a change of scene doesn't change one's nature.
x: 他答應會改，可是牛牽到北京還是牛。

s.p: jiāng shān yì gǎi, běn xìng nán yí
e: a leopard cannot change its spots
s.d: Nature is hard to change; more literary and neutral.
s.z: 江山易改，本性難移，他還是老樣子。
s.y: He is as he has always been; a leopard cannot change its spots.

s.d: Old habits die hard; about habits, not nature.
s.z: 他是積習難改的賭徒，戒不掉。
s.y: He is an inveterate gambler and can't quit.

a.z: 在國外三年，讓她脫胎換骨。
a.y: Three years abroad transformed her completely.

a.d: Turning over a new leaf morally.
a.z: 他出獄後洗心革面，重新做人。
a.y: After his release he turned over a new leaf and started afresh.

牛牽到北京還是牛.u: Taiwanese colloquial saying, often scornful or resigned; mostly about bad habits.

槍打出頭鳥.d: The bird that sticks its head out gets shot: whoever stands out first gets hit first.
x: 沒人自願批評老闆，因為槍打出頭鳥，第一個開口的通常要付出代價。

e: the tall tree catches the wind
s.d: Tall trees catch the wind: fame draws envy.
s.z: 他事業越做越大，樹大招風，麻煩也跟著來了。
s.y: As his business grew, fame invited envy and trouble followed.

s.d: Keeping out of trouble to protect oneself; now often critical.
s.z: 面對不公，他選擇明哲保身，什麼也沒說。
s.y: Faced with the injustice, he played it safe and said nothing.

a.d: Standing out from the crowd; usually positive.
a.z: 她在上百位應徵者中脫穎而出。
a.y: She stood out among more than a hundred applicants.

a.d: Daring to lead the way; for innovation and reform.
a.z: 他敢為人先，開了全市第一家共享工作空間。
a.y: He dared to go first and opened the city's first coworking space.

e: the tall poppy gets cut down
the nail that sticks out gets hammered down
槍打出頭鳥.u: A proverb that explains why no one wants to go first; often followed by "better keep a low profile."

前後矛盾.d: Inconsistent: what is said or done later contradicts what came before.
x: 證人的證詞前後矛盾。

s.d: Self-contradictory; from the story of the spear and the shield.
s.z: 他一邊說要節約，一邊大肆採購，根本自相矛盾。
s.y: He says he wants to save money yet keeps splurging, which is self-contradictory.

s.d: Going back on one's word; reproachful.
s.z: 他答應的事轉頭就出爾反爾。
s.y: He went back on his word as soon as he had given it.

a.z: 她言行一致。
a.y: A good leader practices what he preaches.

a.z: 她對朋友始終如一，從不因對方失勢而改變態度。
a.y: She treated her friends the same throughout and never changed when they fell on hard times.

前後矛盾.u: Common with testimony, statements, policies and rules; also 前後不一.

切身利害.d: Something that directly affects one's own interests.
x: 新稅制和居民有切身利害關係。

s.d: Sharing weal and woe; about shared fate, not only interests.
s.z: 公司的存亡與每位員工休戚相關。
s.y: The company's survival is bound up with the fate of every employee.

s.d: At stake; often at the level of countries or organizations.
s.z: 這項談判對兩國利害攸關。
s.y: The negotiations are of vital interest to both countries.

a.z: 事不關己，他選擇袖手旁觀。
a.y: It was none of his business, so he stood by and did nothing.

a.d: Watching from the sidelines; adds a sense of enjoying the show.
a.z: 其他國家打得不可開交時，鄰國作壁上觀。
a.y: While the two firms fought a price war, the rest of the industry could only watch from the sidelines.

切身利害.u: As in 關乎切身利益; stresses "it affects me directly."

情理之中.d: Reasonable and understandable; within what one would expect.
x: 她訓練得那麼刻苦，獲勝是情理之中的事。

s.d: As expected; not necessarily reasonable.
s.z: 球隊輸球並不意外，是意料之中。
s.y: The team's loss came as no surprise.

s.d: Only natural; more everyday.
s.z: 努力工作換來薪水，是理所當然的事。
s.y: Being paid for hard work is only natural.

a.z: 比賽結果出人意料，最弱的一隊贏了。
a.y: The result was beyond all expectation: the weakest team won.

a.d: Not foreseen at all, often of something bad or big.
a.z: 疫情的規模令專家始料未及。
a.y: The scale of the epidemic was something experts never anticipated.

情理之中.u: Often paired: 意料之外，情理之中 (unexpected, yet it makes sense).

蜻蜓點水.d: Like a dragonfly skimming the water: touching only the surface.
x: 這部紀錄片對這個議題只是蜻蜓點水。

e: try only a little and stop
s.d: Trying a little and then stopping.
s.z: 他對什麼都淺嘗輒止，沒有一樣學到底。
s.y: He dabbles in everything and masters nothing.

s.d: A fleeting, superficial impression.
s.z: 這趟旅行匆匆忙忙，只留下浮光掠影的印象。
s.y: The rushed trip left only fleeting impressions.

a.z: 他對問題的分析鞭辟入裡。
a.y: His analysis of the problem was incisive.

a.d: Getting to the bottom of things.
a.z: 記者追根究柢，終於查出真相。
a.y: The reporter got to the bottom of it and found out the truth.

蜻蜓點水.u: Usually criticizes shallow investigation, reporting or study; can also describe a light touch, as in a fleeting kiss.

情有可原.d: Understandable, even forgivable, given the circumstances.
x: 他是因為車禍耽擱才錯過開場，情有可原。

s.d: Not deserving much blame.
s.z: 為自己的未來多做打算，無可厚非。
s.y: There is nothing wrong with planning for your own future.

e: there is a reason behind it
s.d: There is a reason for it; asks for understanding, not forgiveness.
s.z: 他今天發脾氣，事出有因。
s.y: There is a reason behind his temper today.

a.z: 這名罪犯作惡多端，十惡不赦。
a.y: The criminal did so much evil that he is seen as beyond redemption.

a.d: Can't escape the blame; about responsibility.
a.z: 這次事故，主管難辭其咎。
a.y: The supervisor cannot escape responsibility for this accident.

情有可原.u: Common pattern: 情有可原，但法不容情 (understandable, but the law makes no exceptions).

x: 要留下還是離開？取決於你。

s.d: More polite and formal; implies "I won't interfere."
s.z: 你選哪家飯店都好，悉聽尊便。
s.y: Whether you join us is entirely up to you.

s.d: Plain and direct.
s.z: 價錢高低，由你決定。
s.y: The price is your call.

a.z: 他在公司裡身不由己，上面怎麼說就怎麼做。
a.y: He has no say at the company and does whatever he is told.

a.d: Having no other choice; often resigned.
a.z: 債務壓身，他別無選擇，只好賣掉房子。
a.y: Weighed down by debt, he had no choice but to sell the house.

e: the ball is in your court
取決於你.u: Hands the decision to the other person; 取決於 can also take things, as in 取決於天氣. In speech, 看你 or 你決定 is more common.

x: 這家店九點打烊，人盡皆知。

s.d: As everyone knows; more formal, often opens a sentence.
s.z: 眾所周知，全球最先進的晶片有許多產自台灣。
s.y: As is well known, Taiwan produces many of the world's most advanced chips.

s.d: A household name.
s.z: 這位歌手一夕之間家喻戶曉。
s.y: The singer became a household name overnight.

a.z: 這座古蹟背後有一段鮮為人知的歷史。
a.y: There is a little-known story behind this historic site.

a.z: 他多年來默默無聞，直到那部電影才被看見。
a.y: He toiled in obscurity for years until that film brought him attention.

人盡皆知.u: For news that has already spread; more colloquial than 眾所周知, implying it's no secret.

人情冷暖.d: The warmth and coldness of human relations, shifting with one's fortunes.
x: 失業之後，他才體會到人情冷暖。

s.d: The fickleness of the world; more literary.
s.z: 他失勢之後，才看盡世態炎涼。
s.y: After he lost power, he saw how fickle the world can be.

e: curry favor with those in power
s.d: Sucking up to the powerful; the "warm" side, negative.
s.z: 他是個趨炎附勢的人，只奉承有權有勢的人。
s.y: He always fawns on the powerful and follows whoever holds authority.

e: stick together through thick and thin
a.z: 他們患難與共，始終站在一起。
a.y: They stuck together through thick and thin.

e: help when it is needed most
a.z: 真正的朋友會雪中送炭。
a.y: A true friend helps when it is needed most.

e: the warmth and coldness of human relationships
人情冷暖.u: Often with 嘗盡, 看盡 or 體會; usually a sigh of someone down on their luck.

x: 人無完人，原諒他的小錯吧。

s.d: No gold is pure; often paired with this saying.
s.z: 人無完人，金無足赤，不要要求十全十美。
s.y: Nobody is perfect and nothing is flawless, so don't demand perfection.

s.d: Strengths and flaws together; an assessment, not advice.
s.z: 這部小說瑕瑜互見，有精采片段也有冗長段落。
s.y: The novel has both strengths and weaknesses: some brilliant passages and some tedious ones.

a.d: Perfect in every way; often in negatives.
a.z: 沒有十全十美的計畫，只能盡力而為。
a.y: There is no perfect plan; we can only do our best.

a.d: Perfection; the ideal 人無完人 says is unreachable.
a.z: 這場演出盡善盡美。
a.y: The performance was flawless.

人無完人.u: Used to urge tolerance of others or of oneself; often paired with 金無足赤.

日久見人心.d: Time reveals a person's true heart.
x: 耐心點，日久見人心，誰是真朋友自然會知道。

e: a long road tests a horse's strength
s.d: A long road tests a horse's strength; often paired with this saying.
s.z: 路遙知馬力，他陪我們走了十年。
s.y: A long road tests a horse's strength; he has stood by us for ten years.

s.d: The truth comes out; stresses revelation.
s.z: 案情終於水落石出。
s.y: The truth of the case finally came to light.

a.z: 不要以貌取人，他其實很專業。
a.y: Don't judge by appearances; he is actually very professional.

a.z: 評估應徵者時，別讓先入為主的觀念影響判斷。
a.y: Don't let preconceived notions color your judgment of the candidate.

e: it takes time to see people's true colors
日久見人心.u: Often paired with 路遙知馬力; used to comfort or advise patience in judging someone.

身外之物.d: Worldly possessions; things not worth taking too seriously.
x: 他把財富和名聲都看作身外之物。

s.d: Fleeting as passing clouds; often of fame and the past.
s.z: 榮華富貴不過是過眼雲煙。
s.y: Wealth and glory are no more than passing clouds.

e: be indifferent to fame and fortune
s.d: Indifferent to fame and gain; a positive outlook.
s.z: 他一生淡泊名利，只想把書教好。
s.y: He was indifferent to fame and fortune all his life and only wanted to teach well.

a.z: 她把外婆留下的戒指視如珍寶。
a.y: She treasures the ring her grandmother left her.

a.d: Priceless; often of emotional or unique value.
a.z: 對他來說，這封信是無價之寶。
a.y: To him, this letter is a priceless treasure.

身外之物.u: Often paired with 生不帶來，死不帶去 (you can't take it with you) to urge someone to let go.

事關重大.d: A matter of great consequence; not to be taken lightly.
x: 這次投票事關重大，怎麼強調都不為過。

s.d: No small matter; more colloquial.
s.z: 這份合約一旦出錯，後果非同小可。
s.y: This is no small matter, so please think it over carefully.

s.d: Pivotal; usually of people or roles.
s.z: 搖擺州舉足輕重。
s.y: The swing states are pivotal.

a.z: 我們六點還是七點見面都無關緊要。
a.y: Whether we meet at six or seven is immaterial.

a.z: 這點差異微不足道。
a.y: The difference is trivial.

事關重大.u: Common in official documents, news or when assigning tasks; often followed by 請慎重處理.

x: 銷售數字就在這裡，事實勝於雄辯。

s.d: Evidence as solid as a mountain; about evidence itself.
s.z: 鐵證如山，他無法再狡辯。
s.y: The evidence is irrefutable; he can no longer argue his way out.

e: be plain for all to see
s.d: Plain for all to see.
s.z: 他對公司的貢獻有目共睹。
s.y: His contribution to the company is plain for all to see.

a.z: 他是紙上談兵的人，從沒到過真正的戰場。
a.y: He is an armchair general who has never visited a real battlefield.

a.d: Sweet talk that can't be trusted.
a.z: 別被他的花言巧語騙了。
a.y: Don't be taken in by his sweet talk.

e: the proof of the pudding is in the eating
事實勝於雄辯.u: Used when producing evidence against empty talk.

失之毫釐，差之千里.d: A tiny error at the start leads to a huge one at the end.
x: 動手術時，失之毫釐，差之千里。

s.d: One wrong thought with serious consequences.
s.z: 他一念之差，走上了犯罪的路。
s.y: One wrong decision put him on the path to crime.

s.d: One careless move; often followed by 滿盤皆輸.
s.z: 一著不慎，滿盤皆輸。
s.y: One careless move, and the whole game is lost.

a.d: A small flaw of no great harm.
a.z: 這點小誤差無傷大雅，不用太在意。
a.y: This small error does no real harm; don't worry about it.

a.z: 這兩份提案大同小異。
a.y: The two proposals are much the same.

e: the slightest error leads to a huge deviation
a small slip at the start grows into a big one
the devil is in the details
失之毫釐，差之千里.u: Also 差之毫釐，謬以千里; a reminder that details matter.

首要規則.d: The first rule; the one that comes before all others.
x: 口譯的首要規則，是忠實傳達說話者的原意。

s.d: A golden rule; sounds sacred and unquestionable.
s.z: 「顧客至上」是我們店裡的金科玉律。
s.y: "The customer comes first" is the golden rule in our shop.

s.d: A core principle; neutral, for systems and values.
s.z: 誠實是新聞工作的核心原則。
s.y: Honesty is the cardinal principle of good journalism.

a.z: 我們六點還是七點見面都無關緊要。
a.y: Whether we meet at six or seven is immaterial.

a.z: 別在枝微末節上花太多時間。
a.y: Don't spend too much time on trivial details.

首要規則.u: Often used to introduce the basics of a trade or activity, followed by 是…….

水清無魚.d: Water that is too clear has no fish: expect perfection and no one will stay with you.
x: 水清無魚，你對團隊要求太嚴，到頭來沒人願意跟你合作。

s.d: Nitpicking; an action, while 水清無魚 states the consequence.
s.z: 他老愛吹毛求疵，同事都躲著他。
s.y: He is always nitpicking, so his colleagues avoid him.

s.d: Demanding perfection of others; stresses blaming.
s.z: 對新人不要求全責備，要給他們成長的空間。
s.y: Don't demand perfection from newcomers; give them room to grow.

a.z: 他寬宏大量，不跟人計較小事。
a.y: He is magnanimous and doesn't fuss over small matters.

e: it takes wisdom to turn a blind eye
a.d: Wisely turning a blind eye to small things.
a.z: 有時候難得糊塗，才能保持人際關係和諧。
a.y: Sometimes it pays to play dumb in order to keep relationships harmonious.

e: no fish in water that is too clear
if you are too strict, you will end up with no followers
水清無魚.u: Often paired with 人察無徒; used to tell people not to be too demanding.

殊途同歸.d: Different paths lead to the same destination.
x: 兩位科學家各自研究，殊途同歸，得到相同的結論。

e: achieve the same effect by a different route
s.d: Different techniques, equally fine results; stresses skill.
s.z: 這兩個設計異曲同工，都很有創意。
s.y: The two designs take different routes to the same clever effect.

e: see eye to eye without consulting
s.d: Agreeing without consultation; stresses coincidence.
s.z: 我們從沒交換過意見，想法卻不謀而合。
s.y: We never compared notes, yet we came up with the same idea.

a.z: 他嘴上說要省錢，行動卻南轅北轍。
a.y: He says he wants to save money, yet everything he does works against it.

a.z: 他的做法和公司的目標背道而馳。
a.y: His approach runs counter to the company's goals.

e: reach the same goal by different means
殊途同歸.u: For different methods with the same goal, not ideas that happen to match.

天經地義.d: As natural as heaven and earth: absolutely right and beyond question.
x: 對許多父母來說，供孩子讀書是天經地義的事。

s.d: Only natural; lighter and more everyday.
s.z: 努力工作換來薪水，是理所當然的事。
s.y: Being paid for hard work is only natural.

s.d: Beyond reproach; about legitimacy.
s.z: 她擔任法官以來，言行一向無可非議。
s.y: Her conduct as a judge has always been beyond reproach.

a.z: 用低於土地價值的價格賣房子，違反常理。
a.y: It defies common sense to ignore such a clear warning.

e: be an outrage against all decency
a.d: A heinous violation of moral order; very strong.
a.z: 他竟然對長輩動手，簡直大逆不道。
a.y: To lay hands on an elder is an outrage against all decency.

天經地義.u: Often followed by 的事; can be ironic, implying the speaker takes it for granted.

x: 用低於土地價值的價格賣房子，違反常理。

s.d: Against reason and human feeling; stresses feeling.
s.z: 她要求立刻退款的做法不合情理。
s.y: Her demand for an immediate refund was unreasonable.

s.d: Bizarre beyond imagination; stresses surprise.
s.z: 魔術師最後一個表演實在匪夷所思。
s.y: The magician's last trick was mind-boggling.

a.z: 公司的補償方案合情合理，大家都能接受。
a.y: The company's compensation plan was fair and reasonable, and everyone could accept it.

a.z: 他表現優異，升為經理是順理成章的事。
a.y: Given his excellent performance, becoming manager was a natural step.

違反常理.u: Describes something strange or illogical; more about logic than 不合情理.

未審先判.d: Judging before the trial: reaching a verdict before hearing the case.
x: 還沒開庭就說他有罪，這是未審先判。

s.d: Prejudice; a state of mind, while 未審先判 is an act.
s.z: 評估應徵者時，別讓先入為主的觀念影響判斷。
s.y: Don't let preconceived notions color your judgment of the candidate.

s.d: Believing only one side.
s.z: 主管偏聽偏信，才會做出錯誤的決定。
s.y: The manager believed one side only, which led to a wrong decision.

a.d: The presumption of innocence; strictly legal.
a.z: 法治社會講究無罪推定。
a.y: A society ruled by law upholds the presumption of innocence.

a.z: 這是他深思熟慮後的決定。
a.y: Major decisions require careful thought, not haste.

未審先判.u: Criticizes public opinion, the media or bosses; often 不要未審先判.

x: 那個傳言一定有原因，無風不起浪。

e: there is a reason behind it
s.d: There's a reason for it; urges finding out the cause.
s.z: 他今天發脾氣，事出有因。
s.y: There is a reason behind his temper today.

e: there is a reason for it
s.d: It has its origins; neutral.
s.z: 這種說法其來有自，並非憑空而來。
s.y: This view has its origins; it didn't come out of nowhere.

a.z: 他說他徒手抓到一條鯊魚，聽起來根本是無稽之談。
a.y: That claim is sheer nonsense.

a.z: 這些報導捕風捉影，沒有任何證據。
a.y: These reports are groundless speculation with no evidence behind them.

e: there is no smoke without fire
there must be something to it
無風不起浪.u: Implies a rumor isn't entirely baseless; neutral to skeptical.

x: 他說他徒手抓到一條鯊魚，聽起來根本是無稽之談。

e: make something up out of thin air
s.d: Fabricated out of nothing; 無稽之談 stresses absurdity.
s.z: 這些指控純屬無中生有。
s.y: These accusations are fabricated out of thin air.

s.d: Absurd and outlandish.
s.z: 這個故事荒誕不經，沒人會信。
s.y: The story is absurd, and nobody will believe it.

a.z: 他說的千真萬確，我親眼看到的。
a.y: What he says is absolutely true; I saw it with my own eyes.

a.z: 他的指控有憑有據，不是空口說白話。
a.y: His accusation is backed by evidence; it's not empty talk.

無稽之談.u: Used to dismiss rumors or absurd claims; strong.

x: 她擔任法官以來，言行一向無可非議。

s.d: Understandable; milder.
s.z: 為自己的未來多做打算，無可厚非。
s.y: There is nothing wrong with planning for your own future.

s.d: Beyond criticism; more formal.
s.z: 他的職業操守無可指摘。
s.y: His professional conduct is above reproach.

a.z: 這項政策備受爭議。
a.y: The policy has been highly controversial.

e: be praised and criticized in equal measure
a.d: Both praised and criticized; more neutral.
a.z: 這位導演毀譽參半，卻始終有自己的擁護者。
a.y: The director has both admirers and critics, yet always keeps a loyal following.

無可非議.u: Praises an action or decision; more positive than 無可厚非.

x: 無論怎樣，我們六點前一定要出發。

s.d: No matter what; more formal, for requests and resolve.
s.z: 無論如何，我都要完成這件事。
s.y: In any case, I will get this done.

e: be resolute and not look back
s.d: Going ahead without looking back; about determination, not conditions.
s.z: 他義無反顧地接下了這份工作。
s.y: For her children, she resolutely quit her job without looking back.

a.z: 學會一種語言要多久，因人而異。
a.y: How long it takes to learn a language varies from person to person.

a.z: 這道食譜因地制宜，配合各地的口味調整。
a.y: Policies should be adapted to local conditions.

無論怎樣.u: A conjunction followed by 都 or 也; more colloquial than 無論如何.

毋枉毋縱.d: Neither wrong the innocent nor let the guilty go free.
x: 法院的職責是毋枉毋縱：保護無辜，懲罰有罪。

s.d: Clear rewards and punishments; broader than courts.
s.z: 員工尊敬她，因為她賞罰分明。
s.y: He rewards and punishes fairly when leading his team.

s.d: Enforcing the law as firm as a mountain.
s.z: 法官執法如山，不受外界壓力影響。
s.y: The judge enforced the law firmly and was not swayed by outside pressure.

e: bend the law for personal gain
a.d: Bending the law for personal gain.
a.z: 警官徇私枉法，包庇親友。
a.y: The officer bent the law and shielded his relatives.

a.z: 若沒有人出面作證，這樁案子恐怕冤沉海底。
a.y: Without a witness to come forward, this case may remain an unredressed injustice.

e: neither wrong the innocent nor let the guilty go free
protect the innocent and punish the guilty
毋枉毋縱.u: Used in judicial and disciplinary rulings; a statement of the rule of law.

x: 規律運動能促進健康，這點無庸置疑。

s.d: Without a doubt; more colloquial.
s.z: 毫無疑問，她是球隊裡最好的球員。
s.y: She is indisputably the best player on the team.

s.d: Undeniable; often concedes before a "but."
s.z: 無可否認，他的確付出很多。
s.y: It is undeniable that he has put in a lot of effort.

a.z: 這件案子疑點重重，必須重新調查。
a.y: The case is full of doubts and must be re-investigated.

a.d: Raising suspicion; an action, not a state.
a.z: 他突然改口，啟人疑竇。
a.y: The sudden change in his story raised suspicion.

無庸置疑.u: Also written 毋庸置疑; stresses that the facts are clear and need no debate.

x: 我從來不看評論，無知是福。

e: it takes wisdom to turn a blind eye
s.d: Wisely turning a blind eye to small things.
s.z: 有時候難得糊塗，才能保持人際關係和諧。
s.y: Sometimes it pays to play dumb in order to keep relationships harmonious.

e: out of sight, out of mind
s.d: Out of sight, out of mind.
s.z: 眼不見為淨，廚房我就不進去了。
s.y: Out of sight, out of mind; I'm not going into the kitchen.

a.z: 她求知若渴，整夜都在閱讀。
a.y: She has a thirst for knowledge and reads every day.

e: have a keen eye for detail
a.z: 這位偵探明察秋毫，連最細微的線索都能發現。
a.y: The auditor has a keen eye for detail, and no error escapes her.

e: what you don't know can't hurt you
無知是福.u: Self-mocking or advice not to know too much; sometimes sarcastic about avoiding reality.

x: 他根本沒在聽，這再顯而易見不過了。

s.d: Clear at a glance; about visible clarity.
s.z: 這張圖表一目了然。
s.y: The chart is clear at a glance.

s.d: Goes without saying.
s.z: 健康的飲食會帶來更健康的生活，這是不言而喻的。
s.y: It is self-evident that a healthy diet leads to a healthier life.

a.z: 案情撲朔迷離，警方一時理不出頭緒。
a.y: The case is baffling, and the police cannot yet make sense of it.

a.z: 這篇論文用字晦澀難懂。
a.y: The wording of this paper is obscure and hard to follow.

顯而易見.u: Often opens a sentence: 顯而易見，……; leans toward something being logically obvious.

x: 好的教學和好奇心相輔相成。

s.d: Each brings out the best in the other.
s.z: 畫面與音樂相得益彰。
s.y: The visuals and the music complement and enhance each other.

s.d: Running in parallel without conflict; no mutual boost.
s.z: 傳統與創新可以並行不悖。
s.y: Tradition and innovation can coexist without conflict.

a.z: 他的做法和公司的目標背道而馳。
a.y: His approach runs counter to the company's goals.

e: be as incompatible as fire and water
a.d: As incompatible as fire and water.
a.z: 這兩派人馬水火不容，根本談不攏。
a.y: The two camps are as incompatible as fire and water and cannot reach any agreement.

相輔相成.u: Usually with two abstract subjects; neutral to positive.

先入為主.d: First impressions stick and later views struggle to change them.
x: 評估應徵者時，別讓先入為主的觀念影響判斷。

s.d: A preconception; works more like a noun.
s.z: 他帶著先入之見看這件事，結論當然偏頗。
s.y: He looked at the matter with a preconception, so his conclusion was bound to be biased.

s.d: A stereotype about a group.
s.z: 不要用刻板印象看待年輕人。
s.y: Don't judge young people through stereotypes.

a.z: 越有成就的人，往往越虛懷若谷。
a.y: The more accomplished a person is, the more humble and open-minded they tend to be.

e: hear both sides to see clearly
a.d: Listening to all sides gives a clearer view.
a.z: 做決定前要兼聽則明，不能只聽一方的說法。
a.y: Before deciding, hear both sides; don't rely on a single account.

e: let first impressions color one's judgment
先入為主.u: Collocates with 觀念, 印象 and 成見, as in 先入為主的觀念.

x: 我們的健康和周遭環境息息相關。

e: be as interdependent as lips and teeth
s.d: As close as lips and teeth; often of two countries or groups.
s.z: 兩國唇齒相依，彼此的安全緊緊相連。
s.y: The two countries are as interdependent as lips and teeth; their security is tightly linked.

s.d: Inseparable; stresses structural closeness.
s.z: 語言與文化密不可分。
s.y: Language and culture are inseparable.

a.p: fēng mǎ niú bù xiāng jí
a.d: Totally unrelated; often criticizes forced connections.
a.z: 這兩個問題風馬牛不相及，別硬把它們扯在一起。
a.y: The two issues are totally unrelated; don't drag them together.

e: have nothing to do with each other
a.z: 這兩件事互不相干，別混在一起談。
a.y: These two matters are unrelated; don't lump them together.

息息相關.u: Often 與……息息相關, usually with abstract subjects.

x: 眼見不一定為憑，下判斷前先查證事實。

s.d: Plausible but wrong; about claims or reasoning.
s.z: 他的說法似是而非，聽起來有理卻經不起檢驗。
s.y: His claim sounds plausible but doesn't hold up under scrutiny.

s.d: Passing off fakes as genuine.
s.z: 有些賣家魚目混珠，以假亂真。
s.y: Some sellers pass off fakes as genuine.

a.z: 把照片給我看，眼見為憑。
a.y: Come and see for yourself; seeing is believing.

e: be plain for all to see
a.z: 他對公司的貢獻有目共睹。
a.y: His contribution to the company is plain for all to see.

e: things are not always what they seem
眼見不一定為憑.u: A reminder not to trust appearances; the counterpart of 眼見為憑.

x: 把照片給我看，眼見為憑。

e: see it with one's own eyes
s.d: Seen with one's own eyes; neutral.
s.z: 這是我親眼所見，絕不是傳聞。
s.y: I saw it with my own eyes; it is no hearsay.

e: be plain for all to see
s.d: Plain for all to see; 眼見為憑 is about needing to see it oneself.
s.z: 他對公司的貢獻有目共睹。
s.y: His contribution to the company is plain for all to see.

a.p: yǎn jiàn bù yī dìng wéi píng
a.z: 眼見不一定為憑，下判斷前先查證事實。
a.y: Appearances can be deceiving, so check the facts before you judge.

a.z: 那個故事不過是道聽塗說。
a.y: That story is nothing but hearsay.

e: the proof of the pudding is in the eating
眼見為憑.u: Often paired with 耳聽為虛 (hearsay is unreliable).

言下之意.d: The implication; what is meant but not said.
x: 她說房間「很溫馨」，言下之意是房間很小。

s.d: The overtone; meaning beyond the words.
s.z: 他的話裡有弦外之音，你聽出來了嗎？
s.y: There is an undertone in his words; did you catch it?

s.d: There's more to it than the words; colloquial, often displeased.
s.z: 她話中有話，好像在責怪我。
s.y: She was hinting at something, as if blaming me.

a.z: 她開門見山地說：公司要被賣掉了。
a.y: He got straight to the point and asked about the price.

a.z: 我們就直言不諱吧：這個計畫失敗了。
a.y: She spoke frankly and pointed out the flaws in the plan.

言下之意.u: Pattern: 言下之意是……; points out what someone left unsaid.

x: 現在斷定選舉結果還言之過早。

s.d: Premature; about timing.
s.z: 現在談退休為時過早。
s.y: It is too early to talk about retirement.

s.d: Overhasty; about action, while 言之過早 is about statements.
s.z: 這件事要慢慢來，不能操之過急。
s.y: This matter must be handled slowly; we can't be overly hasty.

a.z: 合約已經簽了，這筆交易板上釘釘了。
a.y: The contract has been signed, so the deal is locked in.

a.d: Success comes naturally when conditions are ripe.
a.z: 時機成熟時，一切自然水到渠成。
a.y: When the time is ripe, things will fall into place.

e: it is too early to say
言之過早.u: Pattern: ……還言之過早; warns against jumping to conclusions.

一顆老鼠屎，壞了一鍋粥.d: One rotten apple spoils the barrel.
x: 一個不誠實的員工毀了我們的名聲，真是一顆老鼠屎，壞了一鍋粥。

s.d: The black sheep; specifically a person.
s.z: 他是公司的害群之馬，老是帶壞新人。
s.y: He is the company's black sheep and keeps leading newcomers astray.

s.d: Years of work destroyed in a moment.
s.z: 多年的努力，因一次疏忽毀於一旦。
s.y: Years of effort were ruined in an instant by a single oversight.

e: a flaw cannot hide the jade's beauty
a.d: A small flaw doesn't hide the jewel's luster.
a.z: 這本書雖有幾處錯誤，仍是瑕不掩瑜。
a.y: The book has a few errors, but its merits still outweigh them.

a.z: 這點小誤差無傷大雅，不用太在意。
a.y: This small error does no real harm; don't worry about it.

e: one bad apple spoils the barrel
a single flaw ruins the whole
one rotten apple spoils the whole bunch
一顆老鼠屎，壞了一鍋粥.u: A proverb blaming one bad member for ruining the group; also 一粒老鼠屎壞了一鍋粥.

x: 我們都替這本書取了同一個書名，英雄所見略同！

e: see eye to eye without consulting
s.d: Agreeing without having discussed it; no compliment involved.
s.z: 我們從沒交換過意見，想法卻不謀而合。
s.y: We never compared notes, yet we came up with the same idea.

s.d: Two hearts beating as one.
s.z: 他們多年搭檔，心有靈犀。
s.y: After years as partners, they are on the same wavelength.

a.p: huà bù tóu jī bàn jù duō
e: have nothing to say to each other
a.d: When you don't get along, even half a sentence is too much.
a.z: 爭了十分鐘後，我明白我們話不投機半句多，便不再開口。
a.y: We don't see eye to eye, so let's call it a day.

a.d: Each side sticks to its own story.
a.z: 兩人對事發經過各執一詞，警方難以判斷。
a.y: The two men each gave a different account of what happened, leaving the police unable to decide.

英雄所見略同.u: Said when two people find they agree; lightly self-congratulatory.

因人而異.d: It varies from person to person.
x: 學會一種語言要多久，因人而異。

e: it is a matter of opinion
s.d: Opinions differ; about views, not outcomes.
s.z: 好不好吃，見仁見智。
s.y: Whether it tastes good is a matter of opinion.

s.d: Adapting to local conditions; about methods.
s.z: 這道食譜因地制宜，配合各地的口味調整。
s.y: Policies should be adapted to local conditions.

a.d: All the same, with no variety.
a.z: 新建的社區千篇一律。
a.y: These ads are all formulaic and utterly unoriginal.

a.p: fàng zhū sì hǎi jiē zhǔn
a.z: 沒有一種教學法放諸四海皆準。
a.y: No teaching method is universally applicable.

因人而異.u: Often closes a sentence as a "no one-size-fits-all" conclusion; 因地而異 and 因時而異 follow the same pattern.

以偏概全.d: Generalizing from a part to the whole.
x: 憑一個觀光客就評斷整個國家，是以偏概全。

s.d: Lumping everything together; often 不能一概而論.
s.z: 每個人狀況不同，不能一概而論。
s.y: Everyone's situation is different, so we can't lump them together.

e: see only a small part of the whole
judge the whole from a narrow view
s.d: A limited view; 以偏概全 goes further and draws a conclusion.
s.z: 光看一份報告就下結論，等於管中窺豹。
s.y: Judging by a single report is like seeing the whole through a keyhole.

a.z: 綜觀全局，這項政策利大於弊。
a.y: Looking at the big picture, the policy does more good than harm.

a.z: 簽約前，我們必須全面檢視整份計畫。
a.y: Before making a decision, review all the data from every angle.

以偏概全.u: Points out flawed reasoning; often 不要以偏概全.

一語成讖.d: An offhand remark that later came true, usually something bad.
x: 他隨口說了一句會有暴風雨，沒想到一語成讖。

s.d: Unfortunately came true; about bad news.
s.z: 沒想到他不幸言中，我們真的被裁員了。
s.y: Unfortunately he was right: we really were laid off.

s.d: A prediction comes true; neutral.
s.z: 那位教授十年前的預言成真了。
s.y: The professor's prediction from ten years ago has come true.

e: fear that the sky will fall
a.d: Worrying needlessly about what won't happen.
a.z: 你別杞人憂天，事情沒那麼糟。
a.y: Don't worry about nothing; it isn't that bad.

a.z: 原來是虛驚一場，煙是從烤麵包機冒出來的。
a.y: It was a false alarm; the smoke came from the toaster.

一語成讖.u: Often 不幸一語成讖; mostly for misfortune.

一字不假.d: Every word of it is true.
x: 他說的話一字不假，全是千真萬確的事實。

s.d: Absolutely true; even stronger.
s.z: 他說的千真萬確，我親眼看到的。
s.y: What he says is absolutely true; I saw it with my own eyes.

s.d: Every sentence is factual; formal, for testimony and reports.
s.z: 警方查證後，證人的說詞句句屬實。
s.y: After checking, police found every sentence in the witness's statement to be true.

a.z: 他轉述時添油加醋，事情變得完全不一樣。
a.y: He embellished the story when retelling it and changed it completely.

a.z: 這家餐廳的宣傳言過其實。
a.y: The restaurant's advertising overstates the reality.

一字不假.u: Stresses that one isn't lying; strong, almost an oath.

有跡可循.d: There are clues or patterns to follow.
x: 股價看似隨機，仔細觀察就會發現有跡可循。

s.d: There are rules to follow; about regulations.
s.z: 辦理手續有章可循，不必擔心。
s.y: The procedure follows established rules, so there is no need to worry.

s.d: It's on record and can be checked.
s.z: 這份名單有據可查。
s.y: This list can be verified from the records.

a.z: 嫌犯逃之夭夭，無跡可尋。
a.y: The suspect fled without leaving a trace.

a.z: 那個難以捉摸的竊賊又一次從警方手中溜走。
a.y: The elusive thief slipped away from the police once again.

有跡可循.u: Used when discovering a pattern; 有蹤可尋 is for tracing people or things.

有錢能使鬼推磨.d: Money makes the world go round; with money you can get anything done.
x: 在這一行，有錢能使鬼推磨，大家都心知肚明。

s.d: Money can even move the gods; more literary.
s.z: 俗話說錢能通神，可有些事真的不能靠錢。
s.y: They say money works wonders, but some things really can't be bought.

s.d: Money is all-powerful; often criticizes a value system.
s.z: 他只相信金錢萬能。
s.y: He only believes that money is all-powerful.

a.z: 這位老縣長一生兩袖清風。
a.y: The old county magistrate was incorruptible all his life.

e: be indifferent to fame and fortune
a.z: 他一生淡泊名利，只想把書教好。
a.y: He was indifferent to fame and fortune all his life and only wanted to teach well.

e: money makes the world go round
有錢能使鬼推磨.u: A resigned or sarcastic comment on how money bends the rules.

x: 這份報告對小公司有失公允。

e: treat one side better than the other
s.d: Unequal treatment; 有失公允 stresses the loss of fairness.
s.z: 老師不該厚此薄彼，應該一視同仁。
s.y: A teacher shouldn't play favorites; everyone should be treated alike.

s.d: Believing only one side; one cause of unfairness.
s.z: 主管偏聽偏信，才會做出錯誤的決定。
s.y: The manager believed one side only, which led to a wrong decision.

a.z: 這位法官以公正不阿著稱，從不偏袒有錢人。
a.y: The judge was known for his rectitude and never favored the rich.

a.z: 好的裁判不偏不倚，不會袒護任何一方。
a.y: A good referee stays impartial and favors neither side.

有失公允.u: A formal criticism, more polite than saying 不公平.

有一就有二.d: Once it happens, it will happen again.
x: 只要開了一次例外，有一就有二。

e: give an inch and take a mile
s.d: Give an inch, they'll take a mile; about greed.
s.z: 你別得寸進尺，我已經讓步很多了。
s.y: Don't push your luck; I have already given way a lot.

e: want more once one has had a taste
s.d: Having had a taste, wanting more; about habit.
s.z: 他靠偷懶得到好處，從此食髓知味。
s.y: He benefited from slacking off once and has since developed a taste for it.

e: let this be the last time
a.z: 這次就算了，下不為例。
a.y: I'll let it go this time, but let this be the last time.

a.z: 今天的會議到此為止。
a.y: That's all for today's meeting.

e: if you allow it once, there will be a second time
有一就有二.u: Warns against setting a precedent, often followed by 所以不能開這個先例.

x: 經理要他說明，這些額外支出有沒有正當理由。

s.d: A just cause for war; figuratively, justified action.
s.z: 他這麼做師出有名，大家都沒話說。
s.y: His action was justified, so nobody could object.

s.d: Legitimate and proper.
s.z: 他以創辦人的身分接管，名正言順。
s.y: He took over as the founder, which was perfectly legitimate.

a.z: 這場爭執師出無名，沒人支持。
a.y: The dispute had no just cause, so nobody supported it.

a.d: Making a scene for no reason.
a.z: 他又無理取鬧了，別理他。
a.y: He is making trouble for no reason again; ignore him.

有正當理由.u: Common in rules, laws and documents, as in 無正當理由 (without good reason).

冤冤相報何時了.d: When will the cycle of revenge ever end?
x: 冤冤相報何時了，我們就此結束這場恩怨吧。

s.d: An eye for an eye.
s.z: 他們以牙還牙，衝突越演越烈。
s.y: They paid each other back in kind, and the conflict escalated.

e: give as good as one gets
s.d: Hitting back right away.
s.z: 對方先出手，我們就還以顏色。
s.y: After being mocked, he decided to hit back.

a.z: 兩位對手冰釋前嫌。
a.y: The two rivals buried the hatchet.

a.d: Repaying wrongs with kindness; from the Analects.
a.z: 他以德報怨，還幫了曾經傷害他的人。
a.y: He repaid hatred with kindness and even helped the person who once hurt him.

e: an eye for an eye makes the whole world blind
冤冤相報何時了.u: A common plea to let go of hatred, often with 得饒人處且饒人.

原著精神.d: The spirit of the original work.
x: 這部電影忠於小說的原著精神。

s.d: Faithful to the original; about content rather than spirit.
s.z: 這齣戲忠於原著，劇情一點也沒變。
s.y: The play is faithful to the original, and the plot is unchanged.

s.d: Authentic and unaltered; also for food and culture.
s.z: 這家餐廳的菜原汁原味。
s.y: The restaurant's dishes keep their original flavor.

a.z: 改編後的劇情面目全非。
a.y: After the adaptation, the plot is unrecognizable.

a.z: 報紙斷章取義地引用她的話。
a.y: The newspaper took her comments out of context.

e: true to the spirit of the original
the spirit of the original work
原著精神.u: Used in reviews of adaptations: 忠於原著精神 or 違背原著精神.

x: 警方的每一個步驟都於法有據。

s.d: Legitimate and proper; broader than law.
s.z: 他以創辦人的身分接管，名正言順。
s.y: He took over as the founder, which was perfectly legitimate.

s.d: There is a law to go by.
s.z: 這個案件有法可依，不必擔心沒有標準。
s.y: This case is backed by law, so there is no need to worry about missing standards.

a.z: 他仗著有靠山，無法無天。
a.y: Relying on his backers, he acts as if there were no law.

a.z: 警察知法犯法，更應重判。
a.y: A police officer who knowingly breaks the law deserves a heavier sentence.

於法有據.u: Common in official statements answering criticism; the opposite is 於法無據.

欲蓋彌彰.d: The more one tries to hide something, the more obvious it becomes.
x: 他冗長的否認反而引人注意，想掩蓋錯誤卻欲蓋彌彰。

s.d: Giving oneself away unprompted.
s.z: 他不小心說漏嘴，不打自招。
s.y: He let it slip and gave himself away.

s.d: Too clever by half; backfires.
s.z: 他想隱瞞，卻弄巧成拙。
s.y: He tried to hide it but outsmarted himself.

a.z: 他的計畫滴水不漏，沒有人能找出漏洞。
a.y: His plan was watertight, and nobody could find a loophole.

a.d: Keeping one's abilities or intentions hidden.
a.z: 安靜的新實習生原來深藏不露。
a.y: He kept his talents hidden, and nobody knew he was the champion.

e: draw attention by trying to cover up
a cover-up only makes things more obvious
欲蓋彌彰.u: Describes explanations that only raise suspicion; often 只會欲蓋彌彰.

雲泥之別.d: As different as clouds and mud: worlds apart.
x: 猜測和經過證實的事實，有雲泥之別。

s.d: As different as heaven and earth; nearly the same, more widely used.
s.z: 兩份草稿有天壤之別。
s.y: The two drafts are worlds apart.

s.d: Completely different; about nature, not rank.
s.z: 這對兄弟的個性截然不同。
s.y: The two brothers have radically different personalities.

a.z: 這兩份提案大同小異。
a.y: The two proposals are much the same.

a.z: 兩個對手實力不相上下。
a.y: The two teams are evenly matched.

雲泥之別.u: Often 有雲泥之別 or 判若雲泥; for gaps in quality, status or level.

x: 烤蛋糕別急，欲速則不達。

e: pull up the seedlings to help them grow
s.d: Pulling up seedlings to help them grow; forcing things ruins them.
s.z: 逼孩子提早學太多，等於揠苗助長。
s.y: Forcing children to learn too much too early is like pulling seedlings up to help them grow.

s.d: Overhasty; 欲速則不達 is the result.
s.z: 這件事要慢慢來，不能操之過急。
s.y: This matter must be handled slowly; we can't be overly hasty.

a.z: 學游泳要循序漸進，不能一下子就下深水區。
a.y: Learn to swim step by step; don't jump into the deep end at once.

a.z: 新創公司要穩紮穩打，不要急著擴張。
a.y: A start-up should build steadily and not rush to expand.

e: slow and steady wins the race
欲速則不達.u: From the Analects; used to warn against rushing.

x: 他的論點根本站不住腳。

s.d: Collapses on its own.
s.z: 謠言傳了幾天，不攻自破。
s.y: The rumor fell apart on its own after a few days.

s.d: Full of holes.
s.z: 他的說詞漏洞百出，沒有人相信。
s.y: His story was full of holes, and nobody believed it.

a.d: Unassailable; often of arguments or defenses.
a.z: 辯護律師的邏輯無懈可擊。
a.y: Her argument was flawless.

a.d: Backed by evidence; a lower bar than unassailable.
a.z: 他的指控有憑有據，不是空口說白話。
a.y: His accusation is backed by evidence; it's not empty talk.

站不住腳.u: As in 站不住腳的理由 or 論點; not normally used of people.

昭然若揭.d: Glaringly obvious, as if held up for all to see.
x: 他想接管公司的盤算昭然若揭。

e: draw attention by trying to cover up
s.d: The harder one hides it, the more it shows.
s.z: 他冗長的否認反而引人注意，想掩蓋錯誤卻欲蓋彌彰。
s.y: His long denial only drew attention; trying to cover up the mistake backfired.

s.d: The truth comes out.
s.z: 經過調查，真相終於大白。
s.y: After the investigation, the truth finally came to light.

a.d: Keeping one's abilities or intentions hidden.
a.z: 安靜的新實習生原來深藏不露。
a.y: He kept his talents hidden, and nobody knew he was the champion.

a.z: 宣判時，他不動聲色，沒有流露任何情緒。
a.y: He kept a poker face and quietly got the plan ready.

e: be plain for all to see
昭然若揭.u: Usually of ambitions, motives or the truth, often negative; not for ordinary things.

x: 「靜心咖啡館」正如其名，環境安靜又平和。

e: be as good as the name suggests
s.d: Living up to its name; also for fame and titles.
s.z: 她是名符其實的專家，不只是頭銜漂亮。
s.y: The Garden City lives up to its name.

s.d: As the name suggests; infers meaning without judging.
s.z: 顧名思義，快閃店只會短暫出現。
s.y: As the name suggests, sugar-free tea is tea without any sugar.

e: not live up to its name
a.d: Not living up to the name.
a.z: 這家「五星級」餐廳名不副實。
a.y: This "five-star" restaurant doesn't live up to its name.

a.d: An undeserved reputation; usually of people.
a.z: 他號稱「名廚」，吃了才知道浪得虛名。
a.y: He bills himself a famous chef, but one taste shows his fame is undeserved.

正如其名.u: Used at the start of a sentence or as an aside, often with names of shops, brands or people.

正義終將伸張.d: Justice will prevail in the end.
x: 耐心點，正義終將伸張。

s.p: fǎ wǎng huī huī, shū ér bù lòu
e: the long arm of the law catches up in the end
s.d: The net of the law catches every wrongdoer.
s.z: 多年後連最大的黑道老大也落網了，可見法網恢恢，疏而不漏。
s.y: However long he ran, the long arm of the law caught up with him in the end.

e: the wicked get what they deserve
s.d: Evil gets its due, not necessarily through the law.
s.z: 做盡壞事的人，終究惡有惡報。
s.y: Those who do evil will in the end get what they deserve.

a.z: 詐騙犯仍逍遙法外。
a.y: The fraudster is still at large.

a.d: A wrong that is never righted.
a.z: 若沒有人出面作證，這樁案子恐怕冤沉海底。
a.y: Without a witness to come forward, this case may remain an unredressed injustice.

e: truth and justice will win out
正義終將伸張.u: Said to comfort or encourage victims and those waiting for an outcome.

x: 眾所周知，全球最先進的晶片有許多產自台灣。

s.d: A household name.
s.z: 這位歌手一夕之間家喻戶曉。
s.y: The singer became a household name overnight.

s.d: Known to all; more formal.
s.z: 他愛遲到是盡人皆知的事。
s.y: His habit of being late is known to everyone.

a.z: 這座古蹟背後有一段鮮為人知的歷史。
a.y: There is a little-known story behind this historic site.

a.z: 他多年來默默無聞，直到那部電影才讓大家看見他。
a.y: He toiled in obscurity for years until that film brought him attention.

眾所周知.u: Often opens a sentence; followed by facts, not opinions.

專家背書.d: An expert endorsement that lends credibility.
x: 這款新產品獲得多位知名醫師的專家背書。

s.d: A celebrity endorsement; about fame, not expertise.
s.z: 這個球鞋品牌簽下一位流行歌手當代言人，打出名人代言。
s.y: The sneaker brand signed a famous athlete for a celebrity endorsement.

s.d: Official certification; more formal.
s.z: 這項產品通過權威認證，品質有保障。
s.y: The product has passed official certification, so its quality is assured.

e: a verbal promise is no guarantee
a.z: 口說無憑，請寫成書面。
a.y: A verbal promise is no guarantee: please put it in writing.

a.d: Talking to oneself; no one else backs it up.
a.z: 他一直自說自話，卻拿不出任何證據。
a.y: He just keeps asserting things without producing any evidence.

專家背書.u: 背書 originally means endorsing a check; common in advertising, sometimes said skeptically.

豬在風口也會飛.d: Even a pig can fly in a strong enough wind: ride the right trend and anyone can succeed.
x: 熱潮那幾年，連平庸的 App 都能爆紅；豬在風口也會飛。

s.d: Going with the trend; a strategy, without the irony.
s.z: 創業要順勢而為，不要逆著趨勢硬幹。
s.y: When starting a business, go with the trend instead of fighting it.

s.d: Plain sailing; not necessarily thanks to a trend.
s.z: 祝你新職一帆風順。
s.y: I wish you smooth sailing in your new post.

a.z: 他創業時正逢不景氣，真是時運不濟。
a.y: He started his business in a recession; it was simply bad timing.

a.z: 這位發明家生不逢時，世界還沒準備好接受他的構想。
a.y: The inventor was born at the wrong time; the world wasn't ready for his ideas.

e: a rising tide lifts all boats
even pigs can fly in a gale
豬在風口也會飛.u: Often self-mocking or cautionary: success may come from timing, not ability; often followed by "but it falls when the wind stops."

子虛烏有、無憑無據、無稽之談、空穴來風.d: Completely groundless; made up out of thin air.
x: 工廠要關閉的傳言純屬子虛烏有。

s.d: Chasing shadows; about rumors.
s.z: 這些報導捕風捉影，沒有任何證據。
s.y: These reports are groundless speculation with no evidence behind them.

e: make something up out of thin air
s.d: Fabricated out of nothing.
s.z: 這些指控純屬無中生有。
s.y: These accusations are fabricated out of thin air.

a.d: Evidence as solid as a mountain.
a.z: 鐵證如山，他無法再狡辯。
a.y: The evidence is irrefutable; he can no longer argue his way out.

a.z: 他的指控有憑有據，不是空口說白話。
a.y: His accusation is backed by evidence; it's not empty talk.

子虛烏有、無憑無據、無稽之談、空穴來風.u: This entry groups several near-synonyms. 空穴來風 originally meant rumors have some cause (from Song Yu's Ode to the Wind), the opposite of this entry; modern usage often reverses it, so mind the context.

自圓其說.d: To make one's story hang together, often a strained justification.
x: 他試圖自圓其說，卻越說越矛盾。

s.d: Arguing the indefensible; more aggressive.
s.z: 他明明錯了，還強詞奪理。
s.y: He was clearly in the wrong, yet he kept twisting logic.

e: act as if it were true
put on a show of seriousness
s.d: Acting as if it were true; about attitude, not logic.
s.z: 他煞有其事地說話，彷彿在宣讀聖旨。
s.y: He talked as if it were all true, but he had made it up.

a.z: 他的說詞漏洞百出，沒有人相信。
a.y: His story was full of holes, and nobody believed it.

a.z: 謠言傳了幾天，不攻自破。
a.y: The rumor fell apart on its own after a few days.

自圓其說.u: Usually in 無法自圓其說 or 難以自圓其說, when someone's account has holes.
